name: Riverbend React Native Standards
description: Riverbend IT's existing React Native coding standards, brought into the platform as grouped checklists in place of a free-standing document.

checklists.name: Riverbend React Native — Project Structure and Naming
checklists.description: Riverbend IT mobile standard: project structure and naming.

items.statement: All the components, globals, images, redux etc.. Should be written inside the src folder
Images should be there in the images folder under the src folder.
Redux files should be written inside the store folder under the src folder
You can create stack navigator file inside navigation folder under src
A folder and sub folder name should always start with small letters and the files belongs the folders is always in pascal case.
Object and variable declaration should always in camel case statement.
Divide The Components (split the React Native components into two individual directories: container and plain components)
Create aliases using babel-plugin-module-resolver to avoid nested imports

checklists.name: Riverbend React Native — Component and State Standards
checklists.description: Riverbend IT mobile standard: component and state standards.

items.statement: Declare The Types: It can either be Flow or Typescript
Separate the styles from the components.
Use Hooks (avoid class based component)
Use Redux for for the store state (Avoid unnecessary use of redux)
Alway assign unique key to each element.
create class component when we have to use state otherwise we should use functional component
Use spread operator. It can make your React code much more beautiful and clean
write your api calls within the useEffect for hooks / write your api calls withing the componentDidMount for class component.

checklists.name: Riverbend React Native — Platform and Experience Standards
checklists.description: Riverbend IT mobile standard: platform and experience standards.

items.statement: Use Platform specific styles.
Always implement as much client validation as possible at front end level
make sure that the app you are building is responsive
DO use Safe Area View to look good on every iOS device
Check internet connectivity for a better user experience

checklists.name: Riverbend React Native — Quality and Release Standards
checklists.description: Riverbend IT mobile standard: quality and release standards.

items.statement: Remove console.log() after debugging, It will make app slower.
Add fastlane set up for automate development and build release process
Use a linter to make your code easier to review.
Lock Dependencies(remove the ^ character in order to lock the dependency on that specific version)
Review your code at least once before creating a pull or merge request

obligationDefinitions.title: Deprecated native iOS and Android APIs must be tracked and migrated before the platform removes them
obligationDefinitions.description: The app bridges into native APIs that the platforms deprecate on their own release cycles. Deprecated usage is migrated before removal.
obligationDefinitions.completionCriteria: Every deprecated native API usage is migrated or tracked to remediation before the platform removal deadline.

obligationDefinitions.title: Every dependency upgrade is followed by a regression run on both iOS and Android builds
obligationDefinitions.description: A dependency upgrade can change behaviour on one platform only. A regression run on both builds follows each upgrade.
obligationDefinitions.completionCriteria: A regression run on both iOS and Android builds passes after each dependency upgrade.

requiredEvidence.title: Dual-platform regression report
requiredEvidence.collectionMethod: Regression run output for the iOS and Android builds.

name: Riverbend Library Catalogue Domain
description: Catalogue management for the library: bibliographic records (title, author, ISBN, subject) and the catalogue vocabulary.

obligationDefinitions.title: A change to the catalogue data model carries a data-migration plan before it is built
obligationDefinitions.description: Existing bibliographic records must survive a change to the catalogue model. The migration plan is agreed before construction starts.
obligationDefinitions.completionCriteria: A data-migration plan exists and is reviewed before the catalogue model change is built.

requiredEvidence.title: Catalogue migration plan
requiredEvidence.collectionMethod: Migration plan document attached to the change.

obligationDefinitions.assurance: Reviewer confirms the plan covers existing records.

obligationDefinitions.title: The search index is rebuilt and verified after a catalogue metadata change
obligationDefinitions.description: Search results depend on the index matching the catalogue. The index is rebuilt and sampled after each metadata change.
obligationDefinitions.completionCriteria: The search index is rebuilt and a sample of queries returns the changed records.

requiredEvidence.title: Search index verification report
requiredEvidence.collectionMethod: Index rebuild log and sample query results.

name: Riverbend Lean Delivery
description: Riverbend's lean delivery practice for requirements, design, construction and test flows.

obligationDefinitions.title: Every accepted requirement traces to at least one test
obligationDefinitions.description: Untested requirements are found late. The trace from requirement to test is checked before a build is accepted.
obligationDefinitions.completionCriteria: Every accepted requirement has a linked test.

name: Riverbend Quality Gates
description: Quality gates for features with business rules or data.

obligationDefinitions.title: A feature with business rules carries test evidence for each rule
obligationDefinitions.description: Loan periods, hold queues and renewal limits are business rules. Each rule has a test result on record.
obligationDefinitions.completionCriteria: Each business rule has a passing test recorded as evidence.

requiredEvidence.title: Business rule test results
requiredEvidence.collectionMethod: Test run output grouped by rule.

name: Riverbend Release Governance
description: Release governance for delivery to production.

obligationDefinitions.title: An app store submission follows a readiness check
obligationDefinitions.description: Store review rejections cost days. A checklist of store requirements is confirmed before submission.
obligationDefinitions.completionCriteria: The readiness check passes before the submission is made.

name: Riverbend Push Integration
description: Practices for notification features that call external push providers.

obligationDefinitions.title: Calls to a push provider are checked against the provider's current API contract
obligationDefinitions.description: Providers change their API terms. The integration is checked against the current contract before each release.
obligationDefinitions.completionCriteria: The integration passes a contract check against the provider's current API.

name: Riverbend Reader Privacy
description: Reader privacy requirements for borrowing history and device identifiers.

checklists.name: Reader Privacy Verification
checklists.description: Verification of how borrowing history and device identifiers are handled.

items.statement: Borrowing history is kept only for as long as the member keeps it enabled.
A member can delete their borrowing history at any time.
Device identifiers are stored only to deliver push notifications.
A device identifier is removed when the member signs out of that device.

obligationDefinitions.title: Retention of borrowing history and device identifiers is reviewed each release
obligationDefinitions.description: Each release confirms that retention of borrowing history and device identifiers matches the reader privacy requirements.
obligationDefinitions.completionCriteria: The retention review is recorded and no retained item exceeds its stated period.

requiredEvidence.title: Retention review record
requiredEvidence.description: Record of the retention review for the release.
